hook.text: A radiation machine gave patients 100x the intended dose. Three died. A software race condition was the cause.

buildup.text: The Therac-25 removed hardware safety interlocks and relied entirely on software to prevent overdose.

discovery.text: A race condition—two processes accessing shared data simultaneously—let operators set lethal radiation levels.

twist.text: The manufacturer dismissed early reports. They assumed hardware was safe. Software-only safety was untested.

climax.text: Therac-25 became the most-cited case in software safety. It changed how the FDA regulates medical software.

punchline.text: Software can kill. The Therac-25 proved it.

quiz.question: What type of bug caused the Therac-25 failures?
